claims.author: B
claims.text: The Time-Machine-only prerequisite branch still cannot satisfy the mandatory external-kit tasks.
claims.evidence: Command: `diskutil list external physical; tmutil destinationinfo | awk '/^Name|^Kind/{print}'`. Output: external physical disks printed no entries; destinations were `Name: tm-blazej / Kind: Network` and `Name: macbook_air_backup / Kind: Network`. Seed grep confirms TASK-018–023 require an encrypted external volume.
claims.test: With no external disk mounted, identify a writable encrypted destination satisfying TASK-018 and TASK-021–023, or require both Time Machine and external APFS storage.

claims.author: B
claims.text: TASK-027's plain factory stop cannot establish global quiescence because active and trigger-less autopilots exist outside its scoped trigger iteration.
claims.evidence: Command: `multica-ctl factory status; multica-ctl factory status --all-workspaces`; source grep of multica-ctl. Output: default status showed one enabled sms-go-tunnel heartbeat. All-workspaces showed `secure-m-systems active Capacity utilization (no triggers — event-driven)`, an enabled heartbeat, and active IBM entities. Source lines 2022–2028 use all-workspace entity pause only when `--all-workspaces`; otherwise `factory_each_trigger _factory_disable`.
claims.test: After an authorized `factory stop --all-workspaces`, require every workspace entity paused and every trigger disabled, including no-trigger entities.

claims.author: B
claims.text: Migrated mkcert and backend private keys remain visible to bootstrap existence guards, so TASK-051 does not guarantee SEC-006 regeneration.
claims.evidence: Commands: metadata-only `find/stat`, bootstrap guard grep, and bootstrap dry-run. Output: `-r-------- .../mkcert/rootCA-key.pem`; `-rw------- ~/.multica/certs/localhost+1-key.pem`; guards only test rootCA.pem and certificate/key existence; dry-run printed `OK mkcert CA present`, `OK backend cert present`, and `0 failures`.
claims.test: Before destination bootstrap, prove migrated private keys are outside bootstrap-visible paths; afterward require different source/destination key hashes and valid destination trust.

claims.author: B
claims.text: The resumability protocol still does not define durable task-level statuses or task-specific no-op prechecks, so A13's claim that PAT-001 bounds rerun harm is unproven.
claims.evidence: Command: `find . ... \( -iname '*state*.json' -o -iname '*schema*' -o -iname '*template*' \) -print; grep -nE 'state.json|completion record|first incomplete|exact blocker|safe retry' seed.md`. Output: schema/template search printed no files. Grep printed PAT-002 `Every phase writes a completion record`, PAT-003 failed-task blocker/retry recording, and PAT-004 `continue from the first incomplete task`; no successful-task checkpoint schema or task-specific idempotency rule was found.
claims.test: In an authorized sandbox, interrupt after TASK-014 succeeds but before Phase 3 completes; give only state.json and evidence to a fresh executor and verify it deterministically skips TASK-014.

claims.author: B
claims.text: A12's proposed `git fsck --full` plus object-count parity still would not prove complete Git equality.
claims.evidence: Current inventory contains 2,263 loose objects and 42 packfiles. `git fsck` validates objects present in one repository; equal counts do not prove equal object IDs and do not cover refs, reflogs, indexes, hooks, or worktree administrative metadata required by REQ-002.

claims.author: A
claims.text: Accept B8. Correct Git verification: compare sorted `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` object-ID sets source->kit->destination, plus content hashes of packed-refs, all loose refs, reflogs, index files, hooks, and worktrees/*/{HEAD,commondir,gitdir}. This satisfies REQ-002 completeness where sampling (TASK-023) and A12 could not.

claims.evidence: Command searched real repositories for an untracked file, computed its OID without writing it, then queried the object database. Output: `repo=/Users/tetsuo/Projects/personal/openusage`, `untracked=plugins/opencode-zen/plugin.js`, `computed_oid=0fcb4ed3126f4d49a7d1de37dee2a13f4f8b0cd0`, `oid_already_in_object_db=no`. claims.author: B
claims.text: The plan does not verify that migrated `tetsuo` receives a FileVault secure token and can unlock the destination at preboot.

TEST-005 checks only username, home, symlinks, and worktrees. Read-only interface check `sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus tetsuo` returned `Secure token is ENABLED` on the source, proving this property is independently observable.
claims.test: Before cutover, run `sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus tetsuo` on the destination and perform an authorized reboot/preboot observation proving `tetsuo` can unlock FileVault.
